notes:
Deep-audit creation path fix: the production schema constraint on the tenant task table was one feature behind the code.

Why: clicking "开始深度体检" (start deep audit) on the production deep-audit page failed with the generic "服务器处理请求失败" (HTTP 500). The production log showed the actual failure: insert into "tasks" ... kind=deep_audit violates check constraint "tasks_kind_check". The tasks table's kind whitelist is a closed CHECK constraint created by migration 005 and extended forward twice before — 025 added browser_audit, 027 added growth_synthesis. The deep-audit feature (shipped in v0.2.24) reuses the same tenant task table, and the code-side TaskKind type already includes deep_audit, but the third constraint extension was missed, so every deep-audit creation on PostgreSQL failed at insert. Nothing was partially written (the insert is the first write of the path; zero rows landed, no cleanup needed), and the rest of the deep-audit feature (navigation extraction, viewing existing records) was unaffected. Local tests and CI stayed green because the default test task store is the JSON backend, which does not validate kind, and none of the five existing PostgreSQL suites covered the tasks table — a coverage gap this release closes.

What changes: migration 052_deep_audit_task_kind.sql extends tasks_kind_check to the seven kinds the code already knows (check, compare, content, visibility, browser_audit, growth_synthesis, deep_audit), in the same forward-only idempotent DROP+ADD form as 025 and 027. No application code changes — the code was correct; only the schema constraint was stale. A new PostgreSQL regression suite (apps/api/test/taskStorePostgres.test.ts) asserts the constraint definition contains deep_audit, creates/reads back/finishes a task for every TaskKind (the list is hardcoded in the test with a sync note pointing at shared-types), and keeps a negative control proving the whitelist stays closed (kind='not_a_kind' still rejected with SQLSTATE 23514). The suite was written first and run red against the old constraint — failing in exactly the production signature (constraint definition missing deep_audit; insert into tasks with kind=deep_audit violating tasks_kind_check) while the negative control passed — then green after 052. It joins the disposable-PG verifier's default suite list (5 → 6 suites, 128/128), and the migration-count assertion in the agent-requests suite moves 51 → 52.

Database: migration 052 only. It widens one CHECK constraint (DROP + ADD on the tasks table, which holds a handful of rows in production); no data changes, no new tables, no RLS changes. v0.2.28 application code runs correctly under the new constraint — it never inserts deep_audit — so a rollback to v0.2.28 images with 052 applied is safe: the constraint is wider, not narrower, and the migrate runner records 052 in schema_migrations and never rewrites applied migrations.

Upgrade note: this is a migration-bearing upgrade — stop the worker and dispatcher containers before running the update (the v0.2.24/v0.2.27 rule); the API container is recreated by the update itself.

Rollback target: v0.2.28 application images only; no data action needed.

Bootstrap: unchanged from v0.2.28.

Validation before tagging, on a clean worktree of commit 804b605 (subsequent commits add only evidence files and this manifest): pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm --filter api test 2117 passed / 185 skipped / 0 failed (the three newly skipped are the PG-gated task-store suite, which the disposable verifier runs for real); pnpm typecheck zero errors; pnpm build; the BFF routing verification 124/124 across the ip, domain and tunnel Caddy templates (real Caddy v2.10.2 -> built Next BFF -> synthetic API); the CI static entry-point and bootstrap-contract checks including the 23 Python retention cases; git diff --check clean. Batch-specific: the disposable PostgreSQL 16 verifier ran migrations twice and the default 6 suites 128/128 both in the main tree and inside the clean worktree; the red run (before 052 existed) failed exactly 2 tests in the production signature and passed the negative control. The main working tree additionally runs 48 tests from another session's uncommitted WordPress files (2165 passed / 185 skipped there), which this release does not contain.

Not asserted here: production end-to-end creation of a deep audit. After deployment the constraint is verified read-only (pg_get_constraintdef contains deep_audit); the real end-to-end acceptance is the user retrying "开始深度体检" on the production deep-audit page.
